key_insight: Real-space energy transfer in turbulence can be mechanically decomposed into local strain self-amplification and vortex stretching, with the spherical neighborhood’s moment of inertia setting the transfer coefficient.
engineering_relevance: This gives a physically grounded way to diagnose and predict forward versus inverse cascade events from local deformation and rotation fields in turbulent flows.
method: Derive an exact local decomposition of scale-\u2113 energy transfer using spherical geometry.
Split the transfer into strain self-amplification and vortex-stretching contributions.
Further separate longitudinal and transverse components to link the longitudinal part to Kolmogorov’s 4/5-law mechanism.
evidence_signal: Direct numerical simulations indicate the derived local contribution captures the dominant energy transfer and statistically separates forward- from inverse-cascade events.
watch_item: The framework is highly geometric and local, so applying it robustly may require high-resolution flow data and careful estimation of strain/vorticity derivatives.
paper_title: Geometric Mechanics of Real-Space Energy Transfer in Turbulence
